beats: Every rocket you've seen throws away half of itself. On purpose.
Because an empty fuel tank is just dead weight.
Every kilo the rocket carries must be pushed faster, and pushing costs fuel.
On a Falcon 9, the bottom part is the first stage: a giant tank, nine engines.
Filled up, fuel is ninety-four percent of its weight. The metal is a thin shell.
For two and a half minutes, the engines drink that fuel. The levels drop.
Now the rocket hauls twenty-five tonnes, fifty-six thousand pounds, of empty tank and engines.
Keep it, and every bit of thrust wastes effort pushing empty metal.
Latches release, and the whole bottom falls away. Tank and engines, gone.
The small top stage lights a single engine. It has far less to push.
Now every drop of fuel speeds up the payload, not an empty tank.
Throwing half away is how a rocket gets all the way up.
